Report_ID: Patients with at least one predefined event of asthma worsening (proxy for moderate-to-severe exacerbation)
Title: Budesonide/Formoterol Pressurized Metered-Dose Inhaler versus Budesonide: A Randomized Controlled Trial in Black Patients with Asthma
Author: Spector, Martin, Uryniak, O'Brien
Comment: Composite definition is broader than "moderate or severe exacerbation" (includes FEV1/PEF declines, rescue-use thresholds and nighttime awakenings). No exact p-value reported; paper states difference was numerically but not statistically significantly lower (Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test adjusted for ICS dose strata). Population mixes medium-dose (69.9% vs 65.5%) and high-dose ICS at entry; counts are not reported separately by stratum.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('BUD/FM pMDI 320/9 µg bid (budesonide/formoterol combination)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (double-blind, double-dummy, parallel group)
Participant type: Self-reported black patients aged >=12 years with moderate to severe persistent asthma previously on medium- to high-dose ICS and symptomatic after run-in
Recruitment source: 46 US study centers, 5 June 2008 to 10 September 2009
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of randomised patients with >=1 predefined asthma worsening event
Outcome variable: Patients with at least one predefined event of asthma worsening (proxy for moderate-to-severe exacerbation)

Report_ID: Proportion of patients with at least one asthma exacerbation (fluticasone/formoterol vs SKP fluticasone propionate)
Title: Superiority of fluticasone propionate/formoterol fumarate versus fluticasone propionate alone in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Pertseva T, Dissanayake S, Kaiser K
Comment: The paper reports an odds ratio of 1.61 in the comparator-versus-combination direction (SKP FP vs fluticasone/formoterol), not treatment vs control, so it was not entered in the odds_ratio field; raw counts are recorded instead. The trial's exacerbation definition combines mild–moderate (PEFR/symptom-based) and severe (additional therapy, emergency visit or hospitalisation) events, so this count is 'any exacerbation', broader than strictly moderate-or-severe. The combination arm (n=146) is shared with the GSK FP comparison row.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluticasone propionate/formoterol fumarate 250/10 µg b.i.d. (flutiform, single HFA pMDI)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: Multicentre (68 sites in Europe, South America and the United States)
Participant type: Adolescents and adults (≥12 years) with moderate-to-severe asthma, prior ICS users
Recruitment source: Primary care clinics and hospital clinics at 68 sites
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients reporting an asthma exacerbation during 12 weeks
Outcome variable: Proportion of patients with at least one asthma exacerbation (fluticasone/formoterol vs SKP fluticasone propionate)
additional_group_ns: GSK fluticasone propionate (Flovent) 250 µg b.i.d., n=146, 75 (51.4%) with exacerbations — recorded as a separate row (second ICS-alone comparator)

Author: Kerwin E, Prazma CM, Sutton L, Stempel DA
Comment: Participant counts are not reported verbatim; group_1_events (59) and group_2_events (70) are derived as the reported percentages (19%, 22%) × the ITT arm sizes (310, 318) and rounded. Report_ID: Participants with at least one predefined asthma event (asthma worsening; proxy for moderate-to-severe exacerbation)
Title: Efficacy of budesonide/formoterol pressurized metered-dose inhaler versus budesonide pressurized metered-dose inhaler alone in Hispanic adults and adolescents with asthma: a randomized, controlled trial
Author: Zangrilli, Mansfield, Uryniak, O'Brien
Comment: Raw event COUNTS are not reported verbatim anywhere in the paper; only percentages (25.2% vs 31.7%) with the randomized denominators (n=127 BUD/FM; n=123 BUD) from Table 1 / Results. Back-calculation would give approximately 32/127 and 39/123, but these integers are NOT stated in the text, so group_1_events/group_2_events were deliberately left empty per the verbatim rule — downstream users can derive them from the recorded percentages and totals if permitted. Also note: the outcome is a composite 'predefined asthma event' (asthma worsening) that is BROADER than 'moderate or severe exacerbation' — it includes FEV1 decline, rescue-medication thresholds and nocturnal awakenings in addition to clinical exacerbation requiring emergency treatment/hospitalization; no separate count for the exacerbation-only component is reported. No exact P value or log-rank test statistic is given ('not statistically significant' only). The trial was stratified by medium vs high ICS dose at entry (mean daily ICS dose 583 vs 607 µg/day) and results are reported for the OVERALL population only, so a pure medium-dose-stratum subgroup cannot be isolated.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Budesonide/formoterol pMDI 160/4.5 µg x 2 inhalations (320/9 µg) twice daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: Hispanic (self-reported) adults and adolescents aged >=12 years with moderate to severe asthma previously on medium- to high-dose ICS
Outcome measurement: Percentage of randomized participants experiencing a predefined asthma event over 12 weeks (Kaplan-Meier time-to-first-event analysed by log-rank test)
Outcome variable: Participants with at least one predefined asthma event (asthma worsening; proxy for moderate-to-severe exacerbation)

Comment: The paper reports the moderate-or-severe exacerbation outcome ONLY as an annualised RATE RATIO (0·47, 95% CI 0·35–0·64) from a generalised linear model, not as the number of participants with at least one moderate or severe exacerbation; the rate ratio is recorded in the general ratio bucket (risk_ratio fields) as it is an explicitly reported relative comparison of ICS/LABA vs ICS alone. The event counts entered (113/437 vs 198/443) are from Table 3 (safety set) for the adverse-event preferred term 'Asthma' (n = number of patients with at least one event), which is the paper's only participant-level count of exacerbation events; this term may also include mild exacerbations, so it is a proxy rather than the protocol-defined moderate/severe participant count. p-value entered as 0.001 because the paper reports only 'p<0·001'. Study was not powered for exacerbations.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Medium-dose MF–IND (160 µg, 150 µg) once daily via Breezhaler') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
